title: The git commands you'll type
summary: status, add, commit and switch, one at a time on the board.

say.never: Most days you only need four git commands. We'll go through them one at a time. A command is just an instruction you type in the terminal.
say.bit: Most days you only need four git commands. Let's go through them one at a time.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

say.never: `git status` asks: **what has changed?** Run it whenever you're not sure what's going on. It lists the files you changed and tells you which branch you're on.
say.bit: **What's changed?** Run it whenever you're unsure. It lists changed files and tells you which branch you're on.

board.code:
git status
git add roster.txt
git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: what changed, and which branch am I on?

say.never: `git add` **stages** a file, which means "put this in the next save point". You choose what goes in, so half-finished work can stay out until it's ready.
say.bit: **Stage** a file: put it in the next snapshot. You choose what goes in, so half-finished work can wait.

board.code:

git commit -m "Add my name to the roster"
git switch -c issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: what changed, and which branch am I on?
put this file in the next commit

say.never: `git commit` **saves the snapshot**. The `-m` means "here comes my message", written in quotes. Write it so a teammate reading the history next month knows what you did and why.
say.bit: **Save the snapshot** with a message. `-m` means "here's the message". Write it for a teammate reading the history next month.

say.never: `git switch` **moves you to another branch**, and the `-c` creates it first. New work always goes on its own feature branch, never straight onto `main`, so the finished robot code stays safe.
say.bit: **Move to another branch.** `-c` creates it first. New work goes on a feature branch off `develop`, never straight onto `main`.

say.never: When a feature is done, you **merge** it into `develop`, which means joining its changes in. If two branches changed the *same line*, git doesn't know which to keep, so it stops and asks you. That's a **merge conflict**. Don't panic: the next exercises walk you through one.
say.bit: When a feature is done, you **merge** it into `develop`. If two branches changed the same line, git stops and asks you to choose. That's a merge conflict, and the git lesson walks you through one.

board.code:
git switch develop
git merge issue-12-add-turbo-boost

marks.label: go to the branch you're merging into
